..
Issued at 235 AM EDT Tue Sep 8 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

500mb ridge axis that has been overhead the last few days in the 
process of being forced south and eastward by a broad, deepening 
Pacific borne wave and associated surface low pressure in the 
process of occluding / closing off over Montana and the Dakotas, 
along with the southern Canadian Prairies. Surface high pressure 
overhead also beginning its dispatching stage right as this system 
continues its north and east progression into central Canada, 
eventually tracking into the James Bay region by Thursday. The 
system's associated surface cold front will gradually be forced 
through the region... albeit slowly... as flow turns more zonal and 
parallel to the boundary. Result will be a 24-36 hour period of 
deep moisture advection into the upper Great Lakes that should 
support atmospheric profile saturation, and perhaps have just enough 
lift in the region to force a convective element into the picture 
too. 

In the wake of the system, ridging and surface high pressure to 
temporarily restore meteorological order amid a cooler and drier 
airmass Thursday and into Friday. Ridging will be amplified by 
another Pacific wave bull-rushing into the Pacific NW / British 
Columbia Thursday and Friday... with guidance depicting this wave as 
closing off and progressing eastward through the northern Canadian 
Prairies into Hudson Bay by the conclusion of the weekend, and 
forcing its associated cold frontal boundary through the region, 
perhaps returning briefly unsettled weather to the region ahead of a 
cooler and drier stretch next week. 

Details: 

Rain / Thunder Chances through Wednesday: Advancement of deeper 
moisture will initially struggle across the region today, with the 
more prolific convective response being confined to the western Yoop 
through the St. Croix River Valley in WI / MN through late 
afternoon owing to better elevated instability... which also 
aligns with where today's Marginal Risk for severe has been laid 
down by SPC. Instability will be lacking across APX-Land this 
afternoon owing to thicker cloud cover hampering lapse rates aloft 
along with low-level dry air suppressing low level buoyancy within 
the profile. Nonetheless, as this deeper moisture plume makes its 
advance, there will be a window for some high-based light rain 
showers. Wouldn't be overwhelmingly surprised to see most areas 
hold dry for the majority of the day, especially the farther south 
one goes... but, the status quo changes in the evening through 
overnight. Core of the deepest moisture finally makes its way 
through the region, accompanied by a pre-frontal warm nose that 
coincides with nocturnal stability in the low levels. 

As such, weak elevated instability (to the tune of 200-400 measly 
J/kg) within a zone of strong isentropic lift to manifest some 
convective showers across the region tonight. As pointed out by 
previous forecaster, thunder chances may be hampered by limited 
buoyancy higher in the profile within this instability plume. 
Convective allowing guidance continues to struggle getting buoyancy 
much past -10C likely places thunder coverage on the isolated side. 
That being said, with such a juiced atmosphere, some of these 
convective showers may be capable of some efficient downpours, 
especially as we go later into the overnight and activity peaks. 
Overall, most areas on average probably see 0.10-0.25" of rain this 
evening through late Wednesday morning... but there can easily be 
some embedded 1.00"+ rainfalls... the coverage of which probably 
holds much more isolated the farther north one goes. 

Trending Windy by Wednesday: Increasingly pinched pressure gradient 
to make its way through the region with this system... initially 
hampered by the presence of a warm nose Tuesday evening / night... 
probably keeps a cap on gusts at 25mph. As the front makes its 
passage through the day Wednesday, increasingly cooler and drier air 
within the dry slow of the system to noticeably increase as momentum 
transfer is maximized. With 925mb flow 25-35kts, certainly possible 
to see some 40mph wind gusts late Wednesday morning through the 
afternoon... especially near the lakeshores and the highest interior 
terrain. Not enough there just yet for land based wind headlines... 
but will need to watch areas near Whitefish Bay as some guidance 
wants to have 925mb flow pushing 40kts up there owing to that long 
Lake Superior fetch. For now, wind headlines will be confined to 
marine zones.
